Iron supplementation in pregnancy and child development

Abstract

Background

Iron deficiency in pregnancy is common in South Asia.

Methods

We followed 1,200 mother–child pairs for five years.

Results

Supplemented mothers had children with higher language scores.

Conclusions

Prenatal iron supports child language development.

Background

Long introduction text.

Conclusions

Iron supplementation during pregnancy was linked with better language development at age five, supporting universal prenatal iron programmes in Bangladesh.

Abbreviations

IFA: iron folic acid.
